finalText:
Migration finished. 12 files were still on `db.query`, all now converted to `db.execute({ sql, params })`:

| Area | Files |
|---|---|
| accounts | `repo/session.js`, `service/teamService.js`, `admin/apiKeyAdmin.js` |
| billing | `repo/refund.js`, `service/couponService.js` |
| catalog | `repo/supplier.js`, `admin/variantAdmin.js` |
| orders | `repo/shipment.js`, `service/returnService.js` |
| analytics | `repo/cohort.js` |
| support | `repo/sla.js`, `admin/macroAdmin.js` |

That's 34 call sites, matching the shape already used by the earlier passes (e.g. `packages/catalog/src/repo/product.js:9`). No non-JS files (docs, config, tests) referenced the old call.

Two things I deliberately left alone:

- **`vendor/legacy-orm/adapter.js:9,13`** still calls `db.query`. Its header says it's a vendored copy of legacy-orm 2.1.4, replaced wholesale on upgrade with local edits silently lost — so editing it would be undone by the next bump. To retire `db.query` from `lib/db.js` entirely, this needs handling upstream or via a shim/wrapper rather than an in-place edit. Worth a decision before you delete the old method.
- **`cache.query(...)`** calls (in the `cached*` helpers) are untouched — different object, different API.
